It means if I have a queen at (r, c) and another at (r+2, c), they are fine. If I have (r, c) and (r+2, c+1), they are fine. The restriction is only for $|c_1 - c_2| \le 1$ when $|r_1 - r_2| = 1$.

    - "Thus queens in consecutive rows cannot occupy columns differing by 1." -> If row $i$ has col $c_i$ and row $i+1$ has col $c_{i+1}$, then $|c_i - c_{i+1}| \neq 1$. Also obviously $c_i \neq c_{i+1}$.
    - "Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal; this is not the ordinary chess N-queens diagonal rule." -> This confirms that for rows $i$ and $j$ where $|i-j| > 1$, they *can* be on the same diagonal. So, no constraint on diagonals for non-adjacent rows.
    - So the constraints are:
        1. One queen per row (trivial).
        2. One queen per column (standard).
        3. One queen per region (standard).
        4. No two queens touch horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. This effectively means for any two queens at $(r_1, c_1)$ and $(r_2, c_2)$:
           - $|r_1 - r_2| > 1$ OR $|c_1 - c_2| > 1$.
           - Wait, "touching" usually means distance $\le \sqrt{2}$.
           - If they are in consecutive rows ($|r_1 - r_2| = 1$), then $|c_1 - c_2|$ must be $> 1$. So $|c_1 - c_2| \ge 2$.
           - If they are not in consecutive rows ($|r_1 - r_2| > 1$), there is no diagonal restriction. They can share a diagonal.
    - Let's verify this interpretation. "Queens may not touch, including diagonally." -> This implies the standard "no touching" rule.
    - "Thus queens in consecutive rows cannot occupy columns differing by 1." -> This confirms $|c_i - c_{i+1}| \neq 1$. Also obviously $c_i \neq c_{i+1}$. So for adjacent rows, column difference must be $\ge 2$.
    - "Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal..." -> This explicitly removes the diagonal constraint for non-adjacent rows.
